newsitem.title: USA: Battle Mountain sees lower '97 gold output.
newsitem.headline: Battle Mountain sees lower '97 gold output.

text.p: Battle Mountain Gold Co said on Wednesday it expects gold production in 1997 to be down about three percent from currently projected 1996 levels of about 930,000 ounces.
The lowered expected output is a result of a decision to phase out three mines earlier than planned, as well as lower than expected production at the Kori Kollo mine in Bolivia.
The company said it will phase out three high-cost mines -- the San Luis, Silidor and Red Dome -- and start production at two low-cost properties -- Lihir and Vera/Nancy.

Battle Mountain also said it is working to lower overall cash production costs for 1997 by between five and 10 percent, compared with anticipated 1996 aggregate cash costs of approximately $220 per gold ounce sold.
The company said it is focused on improving operating performance at Kori Kollo.
